findings.detail: v1.18.0 requires Kubernetes 1.29–1.33; the cluster runs 1.28, which is also already outside the source release's range (v1.17.0): the exclusion is pre-existing — this upgrade does not cause it, but the upgrade is still blocked. Plan the cluster upgrade at or above 1.29 before upgrading v1.18.0. The chart's kubeVersion constraint itself admits 1.28; the narrower supported range is the project's tested-matrix statement (Helm will not refuse the install).

### ACME HTTP01 challenge paths now use `PathType` `Exact` in Ingress routes

> ⚠️ Breaking change

We have changed the `PathType` for ACME HTTP01 Ingress-based challenges to `Exact`.
This security feature ensures that the challenge path (which is an exact path)
is not misinterpreted as a regular expression or some other Ingress-specific
(`ImplementationSpecific`) parsing.
This allows HTTP01 challenges to be solved when using standards compliant
Ingress controllers such as Cilium.

This change is incompatible with certain versions and configurations of the `ingress-nginx` Ingress controlle…

### ACME Certificate Profiles

cert-manager now supports the selection of ACME certificate profiles, allowing
users to request different categories of certificates from their ACME
Certificate Authority.
This enhancement leverages the latest [ACME protocol extension for certificate profiles (IETF draft)][rfc] and is supported by Let's Encrypt and other providers.
For example, Let's Encrypt offers the [`tlsserver`][tlsserver] profile for
standard server certificates and the [`shortlived`][shortlived] profile for
short-lived six-day certificates.
These new options provide users with greater flexi…

### The default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` is now `Always`

> ⚠️ Breaking change

We have changed the default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` from `Never` to `Always`.

Why? Because the old default was unintuitive and insecure.
For example, if a private key is exposed, users may (reasonably) assume that
re-issuing a certificate (e.g. using `cmctl renew`) will generate a new private
key, but it won't unless the user has explicitly set `rotationPolicy: Always` on the Certificate resource.

This change is feature gated and is enabled by default…

### The default value of `Certificate.Spec.RevisionHistoryLimit` is now `1`

> ⚠️ Potentially breaking change

The default value for the `Certificate` resource's `revisionHistoryLimit` field is now set to 1.
This ensures that old `CertificateRequest` revisions are automatically garbage collected, improving resource management and reducing clutter in clusters.
Previously, if not specified, no limit was applied, potentially leading to an accumulation of stale `CertificateRequest` resources.
With this update, users no longer need to manually configure the revision history limit to benefit fro…

### Copy annotations from Ingress or Gateway to the Certificate

We've added a new configuration option to the cert-manager controller: `--extra-certificate-annotations`, which allows you to specify annotation keys to be copied from an Ingress or Gateway resource to the resulting Certificate object.
Read [Annotated Ingress resource: Copy annotations to the Certificate](../../usage/ingress.md#copy-annotations-to-the-certificate ), and
[Annotated Gateway resource: Copy annotations to the Certificate](../../usage/gateway.md#copy-annotations-to-the-certificate), to learn more.

1. We have changed the default value of `Certificate.Spec.PrivateKey.RotationPolicy` from `Never` to `Always`.

   > 📖 Read [Release 1.18 notes](../release-notes/release-notes-1.18.md) for more information..

1. We have changed the default value of `Certificate.Spec.RevisionHistoryLimit` from `nil` to `1`.

   > 📖 Read [Release 1.18 notes](../release-notes/release-notes-1.18.md) for more information..

enrichments.title: OperatorHub packages discontinued; environment installs via Helm/Flux/Argo
enrichments.content: The change only affects installing cert-manager from OperatorHub packages (RedHat OpenShift OperatorHub or operatorhub.io), which stop at v1.16.5. The environment summary shows cert-manager installed through other channels: a flux-helmrelease (chart cert-manager), an argocd-application, a helm-annotation and a helmfile (jetstack/cert-manager). No OperatorHub or OLM source appears in the installed products, though the CRDs dimension is absent. If any cert-manager instance is actually managed via OLM/OperatorHub, the operator should confirm that, since no new packages exist for v1.18.0.

enrichments.title: ACME profiles patch: excerpt too thin to judge impact
enrichments.content: The change patches the forked ACME package in cert-manager to support the ACME profiles extension. It is listed under "Other (Cleanup or Flake)", and the excerpt does not describe any behaviour change, new default or required action. The environment summary shows a cert-manager.io/v1 Certificate and cert-manager v1.17.0 installs, but the installed CRDs list shows only certificates.cert-manager.io, so it cannot be seen whether any ACME Issuer or ClusterIssuer is in use. Missing: whether the operator uses ACME issuers, and whether the release notes describe user-visible effects of the profiles support.

enrichments.title: AdditionalCertificateOutputFormats GA: usage not visible in environment
enrichments.content: The release note says the `AdditionalCertificateOutputFormats` feature is promoted to GA and additional formats are always enabled. The environment shows a cert-manager.io/v1 Certificate and the certificates.cert-manager.io CRD, but the values keys (9 shown, values dimension "partial") don't include a feature-gate setting. The excerpts don't show whether the feature gate or any Certificate `additionalOutputFormats` field is set. Check your Helm values or controller/webhook args for `AdditionalCertificateOutputFormats` and your Certificate manifests for `additionalOutputFormats`.

enrichments.title: UseDomainQualifiedFinalizer GA: impact on this environment unclear
enrichments.content: The release note says only that the `UseDomainQualifiedFinalizer` feature was promoted to GA (#7735). It doesn't say what the feature does, what its previous default was, or whether the finalizer name changes for existing resources. The environment shows cert-manager.io/v1 Certificate and a cert-manager upgrade from v1.17.0, but the values keys listed (9 of 9) include no feature-gate setting. The CRD dimension is absent, so the installed CRDs list is incomplete. The operator should check the upstream PR #7735 and the v1.18 upgrade notes for finalizer behavior. They should also check any `--feature-gates` flags set outside the supplied values.

enrichments.title: nodeSelector quoting fix doesn't reach this environment's values
enrichments.content: The change fixes how the Helm chart templates nodeSelector values (quoting them). The environment's 9 set values keys (replicaCount, webhook.timeoutSeconds, prometheus.servicemonitor.*, global.leaderElection.namespace, global.rbac.disableHTTPChallengesRole) include no nodeSelector key. The values dimension is only "partial", so unlisted keys cannot be fully excluded. Based on the keys shown, the fix does not apply.

enrichments.title: ValidateCAA feature gate removal: no feature-gate settings visible
enrichments.content: The change makes the deprecated `ValidateCAA` feature gate a no-op that only logs a warning. The environment summary lists 9 values keys, and none is a feature-gate key. However, values are marked "partial", and the summary does not show controller extraArgs or `--feature-gates` flags in the manifests. Check the HelmRelease, Argo CD Application and helmfile values, plus any Deployment args, for `ValidateCAA`. If it is set, remove it. The effect is only a warning log line.

enrichments.title: Default CertificateRequest revisionHistoryLimit changes to 1 on upgrade
enrichments.content: The environment uses cert-manager.io/v1 Certificate and the installed CRD certificates.cert-manager.io [v1], so Certificates here produce CertificateRequest revisions. The release note says the default `revisionHistoryLimit` for CertificateRequest revisions is now 1. The values keys set do not include any revision history setting, and the Certificate manifests' spec contents are not shown. Inspect whether any Certificate sets `spec.revisionHistoryLimit` explicitly, and whether anything relies on keeping older CertificateRequests for auditing or debugging.
